## PMO — Coordinating threads

→ [standard](standards-pmo.md)

The state-of-play and coordination thread checkpoints a repository shows, and the responsiveness, reporting and currency of the threads behind them.

- **PMO-1 [M] — the state-of-play checkpoint belongs to the Capital** — A territory Capital, a repository whose declared `capital` is itself, holds the state-of-play thread checkpoint `+/_CHECKPOINTS/_state-of-play.md` labelled `<Space> > SoP`, or `Master: state-of-play` until its change is approved, and no other repository holds one. (standards-pmo.md#state-of-play-thread)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Open the state-of-play thread in the Capital so it creates `_state-of-play.md` there, and remove a state-of-play checkpoint from any repository that is not its own capital through an explicit `ki-checkpoint` REMOVE.
- **PMO-2 [M] — coordination thread checkpoints resolve in the registry** — Each `<initiative>.<project>.md` checkpoint's label ends in its Project in words, as in `KI > Model > ways of working`, or in the earlier form `: <project>`, and on a Capital its Project and Initiative resolve in the `Streams/Projects/` and `Streams/Initiatives/` registry. (standards-pmo.md#coordination-threads)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Rename the checkpoint or correct its label through an explicit `ki-checkpoint` UPDATE, or register the Project or Initiative under the `ki-work` registry standard.
- **PMO-10 [M] — coordinating thread checkpoints declare their role** — The `_state-of-play.md` checkpoint carries `role: state-of-play` and each `<initiative>.<project>.md` checkpoint carries `role: coordination`, or `role: conversational` where the owner runs it as a conversation; no other checkpoint declares `state-of-play`. An existing checkpoint gains the field through its own thread's next update. (standards-pmo.md#thread-types)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Have the thread add its `role` at its next `ki-checkpoint` UPDATE, or ask through the state-of-play thread's messages block; never edit another thread's checkpoint to add it.
- **PMO-3 [M] — active coordination threads are within the cap** — At most three or four coordination thread checkpoints are active at once, plus the state-of-play thread. (standards-pmo.md#state-of-play-thread)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Have the state-of-play thread close or queue coordination threads until the active list is within the cap, removing a closed checkpoint through an explicit `ki-checkpoint` REMOVE.
- **PMO-7 [M] — every record identifier in a thread report is a link** — In every thread report `+/_THREADS/<run>/*.report.md`, each full record identifier in the prose, a work record such as `KI-HARNESS-GOV-187` or a Decision Record such as `ADR-KI-HARNESS-010`, sits inside the text of a Markdown link, and a link that names a record and targets an absolute local path points at a file that exists; a pruned record is linked as `<FULL-ID> (pruned)` to the GitHub link to the file at its last revision. Fenced blocks, such as the reply block, and Needs tags such as `ACCEPT-181` are not checked. (standards-pmo.md#linking-records)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Make each bare identifier the text of a link to its record by absolute path; where the record has been pruned, link it as `[<FULL-ID> (pruned)](https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<last revision>/<path>)`. Fix only the reports of the thread under review.
- **PMO-9 [M-heuristic + J] — every thread folder is trimmed to what is still open** — Each thread folder `+/_THREADS/<run>/` holds only the closed list, `decisions.md` and `<name>.report.md`, and no report whose queries are all answered and whose outcome has a durable home; a report counts as answered when the folder's decisions log names every Needs tag under its Queries, and one with no queries counts as answered. The thread tidies its own folder at every resting point as well as at each mark, and the state-of-play thread names the flagged folders at its own mark. (standards-pmo.md#tidying-the-thread-folder)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — At the owning thread's next resting point, move each stray file to its home under the closed list and delete by explicit path each listed report whose outcome has a durable home, keeping any whose home is unclear. The listing is never permission to delete another thread's files.
  - _Evidence scope:_ The flagged thread folders, their decisions logs and the checkpoints and records the reports name.
  - _Review prompt:_ Does each flagged report's outcome have a durable home, a work record, the decisions log, the checkpoint or a commit, and is every query it raised answered in the log, so that the owning thread may delete it, and did the state-of-play thread name the flagged folders at its mark?
  - _Outcomes:_ conforming; tidy the thread folder; home the outcome first; escalate to owner
  - _Conforming guidance:_ Delete by explicit path only the reports whose outcome is homed; home an unhomed outcome before deleting its report, and leave another thread's folder to that thread, told through its messages block.
- **PMO-8 [M] — the coordinator hook and output style are bound where ki-pmo is declared** — In the runtime-specific Claude Code binding, a repository that declares `[skills.ki-pmo]` selects `"outputStyle": "ki-coordinator"` in its tracked `.claude/settings.json`, and, where the user's Claude Code settings are present, they run the harness `hooks/coordinator-reminder.sh` at `UserPromptSubmit` and `SessionStart` and the style is deployed as `~/.claude/output-styles/ki-coordinator.md`. The user-environment manager, chezmoi, stays the binder; the rubric only checks that the binding is present. (standards-pmo.md#coordinator-responsiveness)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Select the output style in the repository's tracked `.claude/settings.json`; bind the hook and deploy the style through the user-environment manager, such as `chezmoi apply` after reviewing `chezmoi diff`, rather than by editing user settings by hand.
- **PMO-4 [J] — coordinators stay responsive and threads stay current** — A coordinating thread never does substantive work itself, sends every unit of work to a detached background agent and treats an owner message as steering rather than a stop; each turn makes at most five tool calls with reads limited to the checkpoint, `ki agent status`, one report and one short file and writes limited to the checkpoint, the decisions log and a brief, waits only through a detached waiter or monitor, keeps a background check armed while work runs that wakes it at least every 5 minutes, or sooner when an agent finishes, for a one-to-two-line timed update naming the current step of each running agent, with no heartbeat at rest, answers owner messages within one short turn and reports drift in one line; each territory Capital has one state-of-play thread at `_state-of-play.md` doing project management only, keeping the coordination-thread queue within its cap and seeding each checkpoint and opener; a coordination thread works only its Project, follows the bootstrap, keeps its checkpoint current and records approvals before launching. (standards-pmo.md#coordinator-responsiveness, standards-pmo.md#coordination-threads)
  - _Evidence scope:_ Coordinating-thread transcripts, project checkpoints, decisions logs and recaps the owner selects for review.
  - _Review prompt:_ Did the coordinator keep within five tool calls a turn, delegate rather than analyse, draft, edit, test or wait in the foreground, give a timed heartbeat update naming the current step of each running agent at least every 5 minutes while work ran and none at rest, answer owner messages within one short turn and stop work only on an express, named instruction, does the state-of-play thread stay on project management with active coordination threads within the cap and a prepared checkpoint and opener for each, and does each coordination thread work through background agents from a current checkpoint?
  - _Outcomes:_ conforming; delegate longer work; escalate to owner
  - _Conforming guidance:_ Move longer coordinator work into background agents and note the drift in the checkpoint; escalate to the state-of-play thread when a direction touches more than one Project.
- **PMO-5 [J] — threads park tangents, link records and keep checkouts current** — A coordinating thread parks passing side topics as dated one-line items under its checkpoint Open questions, cites and links every record, checkpoint, Initiative and Project by full identifier and local path, and fast-forward pulls affected clean primary checkouts after background agents push. (standards-pmo.md#thread-working-rules)
  - _Evidence scope:_ Coordinating-thread transcripts, status lines, reports, recaps and checkpoints the owner selects for review.
  - _Review prompt:_ Were side topics parked without derailing the work and later homed or dropped, does every mention of a record, checkpoint, Initiative or Project carry its full identifier and a local link, and are the owner's primary checkouts current, with dirty or diverged ones reported rather than altered?
  - _Outcomes:_ conforming; park or home tangents; fix references; refresh checkouts; escalate to owner
  - _Conforming guidance:_ Move tangents into checkpoint Open questions or their proper home, replace short or unlinked references with full identifiers and local paths, and fast-forward only clean checkouts; report a dirty or diverged checkout to the owner instead of repairing it.
